facts.text: simulation.launch includes gazebo_ros/empty_world.launch, spawns the model named panda from the robot_description parameter, and spawns joint_state_controller and panda_arm_controller.
simulation.launch starts rosbridge_websocket with argument port 9090.
panda_control.yaml configures joint_state_controller with publish_rate 100 and panda_arm_controller as a position_controllers/JointTrajectoryController for panda_joint1 through panda_joint7.
panda_control.yaml configures joint_position_controller as panda_simulation/JointPositionController with joint_names panda_joint1 through panda_joint7 and seven gains of 1.
simulation.launch loads joint_position_controller stopped and starts robot_state_initializer_node.
JointPositionController subscribes to the relative name command with std_msgs/Float64MultiArray.
JointPositionController::setCommandCallback assigns msg->data to command_.
JointPositionController::init fills command_ with each joint's position at load time.
JointPositionController::update writes (command_[i] - position) * gains_vec_[i] as each joint handle's command.
JointPositionController::starting and ::stopping have empty bodies.
robot_state_initializer names the absolute topic /joint_position_controller/command and advertises it as std_msgs/Float64MultiArray.
robot_state_initializer switches the trajectory controllers out, publishes panda_ready_state on the joint-position command topic, sleeps 1 second, then restores the trajectory controllers.
The stop callback calls move_group_arm->stop(), logs a message and returns true without checking any result.
robot_control_node advertises constants::service_endpoints::ROBOT_STOP through ros::ServiceServer.
The clone defines service_endpoints::ROBOT_STOP as the absolute name /robot_control_stop.
RobotStopMsg.srv declares no request fields and no response fields.
The clone defines PLANNING_GROUP_ARM as panda_arm.
robot_control_node constructs MoveGroupInterface for PLANNING_GROUP_ARM.
CollisionDetector subscribes to the absolute /joint_states topic with queue size 1.
CollisionDetector.h includes sensor_msgs/JointState.h.
CollisionDetector comments that /joint_states publishes the fingers at positions 0 and 1 and sets index_link_start to 2 for the arm joints.
CollisionDetector's joint-state callback stores the complete sensor_msgs/JointState including its position array.
CollisionDetector skips the first two position entries when it feeds the Panda arm joint group.
robot_state_initializer uses the /controller_manager/switch_controller service of type controller_manager_msgs/SwitchController.
simulation.launch relays joint_states to joint_states_desired with topic_tools/relay.
robot_control_node waits for a planning_scene subscriber and only advertises the stop service inside the home-directory branch after building the planning scene.
When ~/.panda_simulation does not exist, robot_control_node creates ~/.panda_core instead and then iterates the ~/.panda_simulation directory.
CollisionDetector calls /robot_control_stop when it counts collisions for the currently executed trajectory.
simulation.launch includes gazebo_ros's empty_world.launch with its gui, paused and use_sim_time arguments.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
gazebo_ros_control connects its Update to the world-update begin event.
gazebo_ros_control's Update reads the simulation time, updates the controllers and writes their commands to the simulated joints.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.

determinism.notes: Event-driven fake with placeholder joint values and no physics step, pacing, controller dynamics or trajectory execution; it is not a replay of captured ROS traffic

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free rosbridge fake (no Gazebo, MoveIt or physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic stand-in: it answers the declared /joint_states subscription, the joint-position command publication, the /robot_control_stop service and the two companion Gazebo services; it runs no Gazebo, ros_control controller, MoveIt planning group or Panda dynamics
the joint values are placeholders and do not come from a live /joint_states publisher; the fake updates them only when it receives a joint-position publication
the fake never executes a trajectory and never moves the simulated arm; /robot_control_stop only sets a placeholder stopped flag and acknowledges the empty service response

the fake copies a joint-position publication into its placeholder joint values at once; upstream the data only replaces the controller's command_, which the controller acts on only while it is running, writing (command_ - position) * gain to each joint's position interface on every update
/robot_control_stop returns true unconditionally after move_group_arm->stop() and does not reach the custom joint_position_controller, so it is an ordinary request, not the stop
the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports; it runs no Gazebo World::Step

no unpause is offered: on an unpause the trajectory controller resumes any accepted MoveIt trajectory and the custom controller, if running, its stored command_ (joint_position_controller.cpp:38-47); no command value means hold and positions are not observable while paused, so the package cannot clear them first; the operator recovers outside MHS (/robot_control_stop or stopping move_group, the custom controller switched off, then the Gazebo GUI play button or rosservice call gazebo/unpause_physics)

while paused /joint_states (published by joint_state_controller from gazebo_ros_control's world update) and /clock are silent: the joint-state read fails NOT_READY after its timeout (the fake silences it while its flag is set); the device resource reads no topic, so commands and resets do not wait for it, and the joint-position receipt reports the values it sent

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that empty_world.launch opens by default, by a WorldControl message or by any ROS or rosbridge client (simulation.launch starts rosbridge on port 9090); MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)
the read-back needs the ODE engine (empty_world.launch's default physics): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held
the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.8.7 (Melodic) and 9.19.0 releases the companion citations name; rosbridge cannot read their versions
the pinned launch uses the external panda_moveit_config and franka_description packages; their trajectory action, joint limits and robot model are outside the pinned clone and this package

the normal panda_arm_controller follow_joint_trajectory action interface is not declared because the pinned clone does not declare its action root endpoint; the custom position command topic is the only directly cited joint command
the launch loads joint_position_controller stopped and the initializer switches it in only briefly; a deployment must activate that controller before a joint-position publication reaches it

measures.description: Read one fresh /joint_states sample (silent, and NOT_READY, while the world is paused)
measures.name: read_joint_states

operator_required.name: command_joint_positions
operator_required.reason: the pinned clone states no Panda joint travel bound; the joint limits live in the external franka_description and panda_moveit_config repositories, so an operator must supply the reviewed site envelope

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true back: no world update runs, so no controller is updated and no joint command is written; it is the paused flag, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: an operator stops the trajectory (/robot_control_stop) and the custom controller and unpauses outside MHS.
